speaker: Doctor
text: The pain location you described—medial tibia just inferior to the patella—is classic for Osgood-Schlatter disease or Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome. Given your age of 23 and the specific site of pain, this is likely an Osgood-Schlatter equivalent in an adult or early tibial tubercle stress injury. text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter Disease (active tibial tubercle apophysitis).

Given your age of 23 and the specific location of pain on the tibial tubercle without systemic signs of infection, this represents an active stress injury to the insertion of the patellar tendon. The repetitive pivoting and twisting movements during volleyball are the likely precipitating factors for this overuse condition.
